paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^3 (i.e., 1 to 1000). The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 10^0 (1), 10^1 (10), 10^2 (100), and 10^3 (1000). The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and spans from 60% to 80% with major gridlines at 5% intervals. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Base (black circles), FT (blue downward triangles), IKE (red upward triangles), MEND (brown diamonds), MEMIT (purple circles), and ROME (green squares). All lines show a positive trend, increasing in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. At the lowest co-occurrence (1), ROME achieves approximately 74% accuracy, MEND and MEMIT are around 71% and 70% respectively, IKE is about 68%, FT is approximately 66%, and Base is around 63%. At the highest co-occurrence (1000), ROME reaches approximately 81%, MEND and MEMIT are around 79% and 77% respectively, IKE is about 75%, FT is approximately 73%, and Base is around 70%. The green line (ROME) consistently outperforms all other methods across the entire range of co-occurrence numbers.
